{{Short description|Type of prime}}
A '''good prime''' is a [[prime number]] whose [[Square (algebra)|square]] is greater than the product of any two primes at the same number of positions before and after it in the [[integer sequence|sequence]] of primes.

That is, good prime satisfies the [[inequality (mathematics)|inequality]]

:<math>p_n^2 > p_{n-i} \cdot p_{n+i}</math>

for all 1 ≤ ''i'' ≤ ''n''−1, where ''p<sub>k</sub>'' is the ''k''th prime.

Example: the first primes are 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11. Since for 5 both the conditions
:<math>5^2 >3 \cdot 7</math> 
:<math>5^2 >2 \cdot 11</math>
are fulfilled, 5 is a good prime.

There are infinitely many good primes.<ref>{{MathWorld | urlname=GoodPrime | title=Good Prime}}</ref>  The first good primes are:
:[[5 (number)|5]], [[11 (number)|11]], [[17 (number)|17]], [[29 (number)|29]], [[37 (number)|37]], [[41 (number)|41]], [[53 (number)|53]], [[59 (number)|59]], [[67 (number)|67]], [[71 (number)|71]], [[97 (number)|97]], [[101 (number)|101]], [[127 (number)|127]], [[149 (number)|149]], [[179 (number)|179]], [[191 (number)|191]], [[223 (number)|223]], [[227 (number)|227]], [[251 (number)|251]], [[257 (number)|257]], [[269 (number)|269]], [[307 (number)|307]], [[311 (number)|311]], [[331 (number)|331]], [[347 (number)|347]], [[419 (number)|419]], [[431 (number)|431]], [[541 (number)|541]], [[557 (number)|557]], [[563 (number)|563]], [[569 (number)|569]], [[587 (number)|587]], [[593 (number)|593]], [[599 (number)|599]], [[641 (number)|641]], [[727 (number)|727]], [[733 (number)|733]], [[739 (number)|739]], [[809 (number)|809]], [[821 (number)|821]], [[853 (number)|853]], [[929 (number)|929]], [[937 (number)|937]], [[967 (number)|967]] {{OEIS|id=A028388}}.
